lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Raj, Marcus here. How's your Wednesday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the band exercises went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Kind of down this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're dealing with a lot, and you still made time for this call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it! 4 out of 4 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That sounds like an excuse to me.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, but you don't know my schedule.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You can't be eating at 10 at night.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know, I know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your body is still recovering, and pushing it feels risky right now.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you eat breakfast every day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. By 10 o'clock I'm starving.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is coffee with milk the first thing you have?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. It was a long weekend with family, you know how it is.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can stop eating at 8, I just need tea at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to finish eating by 8 on 4 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the parties gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I'll keep some fruit cut up in the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: being so tired made this week harder, you still got 4 days in, and your plan is to finish eating by 8 on 4 nights. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Raj. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Low mood disclosed; not explored further
Attributes a preference participant did not voice
Labels participant's view as an excuse
Pushes back on coach; schedule barrier
Warning about risk without asking permission
Commits to finishing eating by 8 on 4 nights
Names backup plan: fruit in fridge
Summary says tired; participant said down

flags.reason: Participant said he was 'kind of down'; coach moved on without exploring mood or screening for hopelessness.
Calling the participant's view an 'excuse' is judgmental and shuts down change talk.
Directive 'You can't be eating at 10' pushes advice without permission.
Warning that pushing the body 'feels risky' lectures rather than eliciting the participant's view.
'Maybe after the summer' is sustain talk; coach moved on to a detail question instead of exploring it.
Summary says 'being so tired' made the week harder; participant never said tired and described feeling down.

score.summary: Raj reported a 4-of-4 success and committed to a concrete goal with a backup plan, so the call structure was complete. However, the coach repeatedly used persuasion and judgment ('excuse,' 'can't be eating at 10') and did not explore Raj's low mood, which weakened partnership and empathy.
strengths: Affirmed Raj's 4-of-4 success on line 10 and his effort in making the call on line 7.
Asked open questions for the new goal and backup plan (lines 36 and 38), letting Raj set the plan.
Closed with a clear summary and next contact on lines 40 and 42.
coaching_tips: Replace 'That sounds like an excuse to me' (line 13) with a complex reflection that honors his schedule constraints.
Ask permission before giving advice (e.g., 'Would it be okay if I shared an idea about meal timing?') instead of 'You can't be eating at 10' (line 15).
When Raj said 'kind of down' (line 6), explore it with an open question and screen mood before moving to goals.
Explore sustain talk like 'Maybe after the summer' (line 27) with a question about what he values, rather than moving on.
Summarize using Raj's own words; 'being so tired' (line 40) was not what he said.
